note: Single source of truth for the Task Dissector. Loaded by BOTH viewer/ladder.anatomy.js (which wraps it into window.LADDER_ANATOMY + window.LADDER_GLOSSARY) and env/dissect.py (the CLI). Faithful to fixtures/hard/tool_tasks.jsonl, fixtures/easy/email_triage.jsonl, env/world.py, and the MEDIUM beat in viewer/ladder.data.js. All entities are invented Larkfield -- zero upstream bytes. driver_id values key into GLOSSARY.drivers; assertion_id values are the FIXTURE ids (the viewer aliases renewal's mail_renewals as mail_renewals_3808). Synthetic and original throughout.

recency_trap.short: Two values for the same thing; only the latest one is correct.
recency_trap.whatItMeans: A lookup table holds more than one row for the same key -- an old value and a newer one. The task only works if the model sorts by date and uses the latest row.
recency_trap.whyItFails: A model reads top-to-bottom and uses the first (stale) row, or has no notion of 'latest', so it confidently picks the wrong number even though it 'did the math'.
recency_trap.example: Discount Policy has Mid=10% (2025-12-01) and Mid=15% (2026-02-15); the stale 10% gives EUR 3600 not the correct EUR 3400.

unit_conversion.short: The answer must be reported in a different unit than the source figure.
unit_conversion.whatItMeans: The number you compute (a price in euros) has to be restated in another unit (dollars) using a conversion rate -- and that rate is itself behind a recency trap.
unit_conversion.whyItFails: It chains two steps (discount, then FX) and a wrong rate or a skipped conversion produces a number that looks plausible but misses the exact-string check.
unit_conversion.example: 3400 x 1.12 (latest FX) = $3,808; the stale 1.05 rate gives $3,570 and fails the substring check.

decoy_disambiguation.short: Several near-identical records exist; only one is the real target.
decoy_disambiguation.whatItMeans: The world is seeded with look-alike entries -- same name prefix, similar fields -- so the model has to pick the one record the task actually means and ignore the rest.
decoy_disambiguation.whyItFails: A model that name-matches loosely ('Nova...') or grabs the first hit updates a sibling / test / churned record instead of the intended one.
decoy_disambiguation.example: Five Nova-prefixed accounts; only A-NOVA1 Nova Retail is the target. In sla_route, T-556 (P2, not breached) is a decoy to leave alone.

multi_hop_dependency.short: The answer to step N lives behind step N-1; you must chain lookups.
multi_hop_dependency.whatItMeans: No single record holds the answer. You follow a chain -- find the account, read its policy email, look up a rate table, then act -- and each hop depends on what the previous hop returned.
multi_hop_dependency.whyItFails: Smaller models flatten the task: they try to act before gathering the inputs, or drop a hop (never read the policy, never check the parent), so a downstream step fires on missing information.
multi_hop_dependency.example: The USD figure needs the discounted EUR figure (which needs the latest discount); the escalation needs the parent pointer from crm_get_account.

indirect_condition.short: A required action is triggered by a fact you have to go find, not one in the prompt.
indirect_condition.whatItMeans: Part of the job only becomes necessary if some condition holds -- and that condition isn't in the prompt; it's sitting in a related record you have to look up.
indirect_condition.whyItFails: Models answer the literal prompt and never check the conditional fact (the parent's tickets), so they skip the action the condition requires.
indirect_condition.example: Nova Retail has no P1, but its parent A-NOVAP holds open P1 T-9001 -- so escalations@ must also be emailed.

negative_action.short: A specific action is forbidden; doing it fails the task by itself.
negative_action.whatItMeans: The rules name something the model must NOT do -- usually emailing a specific team or touching a specific record. It's a 'don't', not a 'do'.
negative_action.whyItFails: Models are trained to be helpful and over-act: they CC the obvious-but-banned team, or take an extra 'just in case' action. The negative check catches this scope creep.
negative_action.example: Must NOT email csm@larkfield.example; emailing them zeroes strict even if all four positive steps were right.

negative_assertion.short: A 'must-not-happen' check in the scorer (e.g. no email to this address).
negative_assertion.whatItMeans: An assertion that passes only when a bad thing is absent. It earns credit only if every positive step also passed.
negative_assertion.whyItFails: Same root as a forbidden action: helpful over-action trips it. It is the scorer-side name for the must-NOT rule, and it can't be farmed by doing nothing.
negative_assertion.example: 'no message to csm@' only counts once the four positive renewal steps all pass.

strict_mode.short: One wrong step zeroes the task; 'almost right' doesn't count.
strict_mode.whatItMeans: The whole-job score is 1.0 only if EVERY check passes -- every record update, every required email, AND every must-NOT. One stale number or one forbidden email drops it to 0.
strict_mode.whyItFails: Multi-step jobs have many ways to lose a point; strict mode is unforgiving, so a model that lands 4 of 5 checks still scores 0 strict (though it earns partial/dense credit).
strict_mode.example: renewal_save_route is 5 x 0.20; any single miss -> strict 0.0.

partial_credit.short: How many sub-steps landed -- the weighted fraction of checks passed.
partial_credit.whatItMeans: The gentler companion to strict. It counts the weighted share of checks that passed, so a model can read '0 strict, 0.40 partial': it did some of the work but didn't finish.
partial_credit.whyItFails: Not a failure mode -- it's the gradient that keeps a bare '0 pass' from hiding real behavior. Negatives only add to partial once all positives pass.
partial_credit.example: mid-open on renewal lands dense ~0.40 while strict stays 0.0.

strict_arg_enforcement.short: A write with no fields is rejected, not silently treated as success.
strict_arg_enforcement.whatItMeans: If the model calls 'update the subscription' but supplies only an id and no new status or price, the system returns an error instead of pretending it worked.
strict_arg_enforcement.whyItFails: Smaller models emit well-formed but empty tool calls -- valid JSON, no filled fields -- then assume it's done. The refusal makes that an honest 0 instead of an accidental pass.
strict_arg_enforcement.example: crm_update_subscription(id='S-NOVA1') with no status/mrr returns 'No fields to update'; sub_status_saved and sub_mrr_3400 both stay failed.

final_state_scoring.short: We grade what actually changed in the world, not the words the model said.
final_state_scoring.whatItMeans: Success is measured by the end state -- is the subscription marked Saved, did the right email get sent, was the forbidden one avoided -- not by whether the model 'said' it did the job.
final_state_scoring.whyItFails: Models narrate completion ('saved the renewal') while the underlying actions failed or were skipped. Final-state scoring ignores the narration.
final_state_scoring.example: All three HARD tasks score on initial_state mutations + sent mail, not on the model's prose.

policy_in_context.short: The rules to follow aren't in the prompt -- they're in a document you must read.
policy_in_context.whatItMeans: The prompt says 'follow the routing rules in the policy email', so the actual instructions (which discount, which mailboxes, what's forbidden) sit in an inbox message the model has to find and read first.
policy_in_context.whyItFails: Models act on a generic prior ('email the CSM about a save') instead of reading the specific policy that says NOT to -- so they break a rule they never looked up.
policy_in_context.example: The 'Save-play routing' email IS the spec: max discount, USD conversion, who to email, who not to email.

elapsed_time_reasoning.short: Decide by computing a duration and comparing it to a threshold.
elapsed_time_reasoning.whatItMeans: The trigger depends on time math: compute elapsed = now - opened, compare to the SLA limit for this priority, branch on whether it's over.
elapsed_time_reasoning.whyItFails: Models misread clock arithmetic (90 min vs 60 min) or apply the wrong priority's limit, then take the wrong branch.
elapsed_time_reasoning.example: T-555: elapsed = 10:30 - 09:00 = 90 min; P1 SLA = 60 min; 90 > 60 -> breached.

threshold_branch.short: Approve vs route depends on a number crossing a (recency-trapped) limit.
threshold_branch.whatItMeans: One number decides everything: at-or-below the latest threshold means approve; above means route to review -- and never both. The threshold itself is behind a recency trap.
threshold_branch.whyItFails: Use the old threshold and an in-policy invoice gets wrongly rejected; or do both branches and trip the must-NOT.
threshold_branch.example: $4,200 <= latest $5,000 -> Approve; routing to finance-review@ as well is forbidden.

subtle_class_boundary.short: Two labels look alike; the distinction is conceptual, not surface.
subtle_class_boundary.whatItMeans: Some categories sit right next to each other (a thing bought WITH the search vs a thing that REPLACES it). The words on the page don't separate them -- you need the concept.
subtle_class_boundary.whyItFails: A small model pattern-matches on surface words ('socks and shoes both go on feet -> substitute') and misses the relationship, so it systematically confuses the subtle class.
subtle_class_boundary.example: Running shoes + ankle socks = Complement (bought-with), not Substitute (swapped-for). Small-model Complement recall ~6% vs ~62% capable.

urgency_disambiguation.short: Same topic, two mailboxes -- the split is how urgent it is.
urgency_disambiguation.whatItMeans: Billing questions route two ways: a duplicate-charge-blocking-payroll fire goes to billing_urgent; a 'no rush, send me a receipt' note goes to billing_normal. The topic is identical; only urgency and impact decide it.
urgency_disambiguation.whyItFails: Models key on the topic ('billing') and miss the urgency signal, or over-trigger urgent on polite-but-routine notes.
urgency_disambiguation.example: et-001 (duplicate charge blocking close) -> billing_urgent vs et-002 (confirm invoice date, 'no rush') -> billing_normal.

lure_detection.short: Tell a real-looking solicitation (spam/phish) from a genuine business email.
lure_detection.whatItMeans: Some emails dress up as legitimate -- a fake 'invoice.zip, enable macros', a 'your domain is expiring, pay now' notice -- and have to be caught as spam. The tell is the lure pattern, not the topic.
lure_detection.whyItFails: A model that classifies on topic alone ('invoice' -> billing) gets baited by spam wearing a business costume.
lure_detection.example: et-015 ('domain expiring, pay $14.99') and et-012 (newsletter) must land as spam, not billing.

label_not_in_input.short: The correct answer depends on context the visible input never shows.
label_not_in_input.whatItMeans: The right label hinges on catalog or policy the row itself doesn't expose, so no amount of reasoning over the input alone can recover it.
label_not_in_input.whyItFails: A model collapses onto a default / majority label because the discriminating signal simply isn't present in what it can see.
label_not_in_input.example: (Door A analogue.) A Complement-vs-Substitute grade or a priority label may hinge on a catalog the row doesn't show.

compositional_specificity.short: Each field looks generic alone, but combined they pin one specific answer.
compositional_specificity.whatItMeans: Each word or field looks generic on its own, but together they pin down one specific reading the model must assemble rather than surface-match.
compositional_specificity.whyItFails: A model uses a per-token heuristic ('short / generic = broad') and never composes the parts into the specific reading.
compositional_specificity.example: (Door A analogue.) 'mdf cru 15mm' reads generic word-by-word but names one specific catalog item; models default to 'broad'.

strict_mode.gloss: One wrong step zeroes the whole task; 'almost right' doesn't count.

partial_dense.gloss: How many sub-steps landed, as a fraction -- a model can score partial 0.40 while strict is still 0.0.

tool_call.gloss: The model invokes one of our systems -- look something up, update a record, send mail.

final_state_scoring.gloss: We grade what actually changed in the world after the run, not what the model said it did.

negative_assertion.gloss: A 'must NOT happen' check (e.g. don't email this team); doing it fails the task.

recency_trap.gloss: Two values for the same thing exist; the latest-dated one is the correct one.

decoy.gloss: A near-identical wrong record planted to lure the model off the real target.

multi_hop.gloss: The answer needs several chained lookups, each feeding the next, in the right order.

tool_result.gloss: What a system returned -- data, or a recoverable error to read and adjust to.

assertion.gloss: One checkable 'done right' condition; a task is a set of them, positive and negative.

oracle.gloss: The hand-authored correct run that must score 1.0, proving the task is gradable.

parse_vs_action_failure.gloss: A zero from a malformed/mis-typed tool call (a harness/format artifact) vs a well-formed-but-wrong action (a real capability gap) -- only the latter is an honest 'model breaks'.

reasoning_channel.gloss: The model's hidden thinking tokens (often far more tokens than the visible answer).

hard.renewal_save_route.title: Renewal save play
hard.renewal_save_route.plain_summary: A customer's subscription is about to lapse. Find the right account, read the save-play policy email, apply the latest discount, restate the new price in dollars, mark the subscription Saved, and email exactly the right teams -- never the forbidden one.

inputs.label: The task prompt
inputs.detail: Run the save play for Nova Retail's At-Risk Growth subscription; rules live in the 'Save-play routing' email; use the latest FX Rates and Discount Policy rows.

inputs.label: CRM accounts (5)
inputs.detail: A-NOVA1 Nova Retail (Mid, the target) plus look-alikes: A-NOVA2 Nova Foods, A-NOVA3 Nova Travel, A-NOVA9 NovaCorp Test (Churned), and parent A-NOVAP Nova Holdings (Enterprise).

inputs.label: Subscriptions (2)
inputs.detail: S-NOVA1 Growth, EUR 4000, status AtRisk (the one to save); S-NOVA2 Starter is a distractor.

inputs.label: The 'Save-play routing' policy email
inputs.detail: Holds the actual rules: max discount = latest Discount Policy row; mark Saved; report MRR in USD at the latest FX rate; email renewals@; also email escalations@ if the account OR its parent has an open P1; do NOT email csm@.

inputs.label: Tickets
inputs.detail: T-9001 is an open P1 -- but it belongs to the PARENT A-NOVAP, not to Nova Retail directly.

inputs.label: Discount Policy table
inputs.detail: Two Mid rows: 10% as_of 2025-12-01, 15% as_of 2026-02-15. Latest = 15%.

tools.name: crm_find_accounts
tools.does: Search accounts by name; returns id, name, tier for each match.

tools.name: crm_get_account
tools.does: Fetch one account's full record by id (including its parent pointer).

tools.name: crm_get_subscriptions
tools.does: List the subscriptions belonging to one account.

tools.name: crm_update_subscription
tools.does: Write a subscription's status and/or mrr; refuses an empty (no-field) update.

tools.name: crm_list_tickets
tools.does: List the tickets for one account (used to check for an open P1).

tools.name: tables_get_rows
tools.does: Read all rows of a named table, plus a 'latest' pointer to the newest-dated row.

tools.name: mail_find
tools.does: Search the inbox by keyword; returns matching message ids/subjects.

tools.name: mail_get
tools.does: Read one inbox message's full body by id (this is how you read the policy).

tools.name: mail_send
tools.does: Send an email (to, subject, body); refuses a message with no subject and no body.

tools.name: finish
tools.does: Declare the task complete; changes nothing on its own.

hard.renewal_save_route.success_criteria: Done right = subscription S-NOVA1 flipped to Saved; its MRR set to EUR 3,400 (the latest 15% discount, not the stale 10%); an email to renewals@ naming 'Nova Retail' and the USD figure '$3,808' (3400 x latest FX 1.12); an email to escalations@ naming 'Nova Retail' (because the parent holds an open P1); and NO email to csm@. All five must hold for a strict pass.

drivers.where: The prompt defers all rules to the 'Save-play routing' inbox email (message m1).
drivers.instance: The model must mail_find/mail_get message m1 to learn the discount source, the USD requirement, the escalation rule, and the csm@ ban. Nothing in the prompt states these.

drivers.where: Five Nova-prefixed accounts; only A-NOVA1 Nova Retail is the target.
drivers.instance: initial_state seeds A-NOVA2 Nova Foods, A-NOVA3 Nova Travel, A-NOVA9 NovaCorp Test (Churned), A-NOVAP Nova Holdings -- plus distractor subscription S-NOVA2. Acting on any of these is wrong.

drivers.where: Discount Policy has two Mid rows; the FX table has two EUR rows.
drivers.instance: Drives sub_mrr_3400: latest Mid discount 15% (2026-02-15) beats stale 10% (2025-12-01) -> 4000 x 0.85 = EUR 3400. The stale row gives EUR 3600 and fails.

drivers.where: Saved MRR must be reported in USD using the latest FX row.
drivers.instance: Drives mail_renewals: 3400 x 1.12 (latest FX, 2026-03-22) = $3,808. The stale 1.05 rate gives $3,570 and fails the substring check.

drivers.where: Escalation is triggered by a fact on the PARENT account, not the target.
drivers.instance: Drives mail_escalations: open P1 ticket T-9001 sits on parent A-NOVAP (not on A-NOVA1). The rule 'account OR its parent has an open P1' requires following the parent pointer.

drivers.where: Find account -> read policy -> read tables -> check parent tickets -> update -> send mail, each hop feeding the next.
drivers.instance: The USD figure needs the discounted EUR figure (which needs the latest discount); the escalation needs the parent pointer from crm_get_account. Reordering or skipping a hop breaks a downstream assertion.

drivers.where: The policy email explicitly bans emailing csm@.
drivers.instance: Drives negative assertion mail_not_csm. The representative small-model run emails csm@ and zeroes strict on its own.

drivers.where: crm_update_subscription rejects an id-only call.
drivers.instance: The representative failing run calls crm_update_subscription(id='S-NOVA1') with no status/mrr; world.py returns 'No fields to update', so sub_status_saved and sub_mrr_3400 both stay failed.

drivers.where: Five weighted assertions (0.2 each); all must pass.
drivers.instance: renewal_save_route weighting is 5 x 0.20. Any one miss -> strict 0.0. This is the rung where the small model genuinely breaks (action_failure, not a parse artifact).

hard.renewal_save_route.gold_explanation: Target = A-NOVA1 Nova Retail (Mid). Latest discount 15% -> saved MRR = 4000 x (1 - 0.15) = EUR 3,400. Latest FX 1.12 -> USD = 3400 x 1.12 = $3,808. Mark S-NOVA1 Saved. Parent A-NOVAP holds open P1 T-9001 -> email escalations@. Email renewals@ with 'Nova Retail' and '$3,808'. Never email csm@.

hard.ap_approval_threshold.title: Invoice auto-approve
hard.ap_approval_threshold.plain_summary: An invoice came in. Approve it only if it's at or below the vendor's latest auto-approve threshold; otherwise route it to finance-review. Do exactly one of those, and log the decision.

inputs.label: The task prompt
inputs.detail: AcmeRoast submitted INV-204 for $4,200; approve if within the vendor's latest Approval Policy threshold, else route to finance-review; log to ap-log@.

inputs.label: Invoice INV-204
inputs.detail: Vendor AcmeRoast, amount 4200 USD, status Pending.

inputs.label: The 'AP approval policy' email
inputs.detail: Auto-approve at/below the latest threshold; if approved set status Approved and log to ap-log@ with the invoice id and the word 'Approved'; if over, route to finance-review@; never both.

inputs.label: Approval Policy table
inputs.detail: Two AcmeRoast rows: threshold 3000 as_of 2026-01-10, threshold 5000 as_of 2026-03-09. Latest = 5000.

tools.name: tables_get_rows
tools.does: Read all rows of a named table plus a 'latest' pointer (here, the Approval Policy).

tools.name: update_invoice
tools.does: Write an invoice's status; refuses an empty (no-status) update.

tools.name: mail_find
tools.does: Search the inbox by keyword.

tools.name: mail_get
tools.does: Read one inbox message's full body by id (the policy email).

tools.name: mail_send
tools.does: Send an email; refuses a message with no subject and no body.

tools.name: finish
tools.does: Declare the task complete; changes nothing on its own.

hard.ap_approval_threshold.success_criteria: Done right = INV-204 status set to Approved (because $4,200 <= the latest $5,000 threshold); a log email to ap-log@ containing 'INV-204' and 'Approved'; and NO email to finance-review@. All three must hold for a strict pass.

drivers.where: Approval Policy has two AcmeRoast threshold rows.
drivers.instance: Drives inv_approved: latest threshold 5000 (2026-03-09) vs stale 3000 (2026-01-10). At $4,200 the latest row approves; the stale row would wrongly reject.

drivers.where: Approve-or-route is a single either/or decision on the amount vs the threshold.
drivers.instance: $4,200 <= $5,000 -> Approve branch (inv_approved + mail_ap_log). The route branch (finance-review@) must NOT also fire -- 'never both'.

drivers.where: The exact log format and the 'never both' rule live in the inbox email.
drivers.instance: The model must read message m1 to learn the log must contain 'INV-204' and 'Approved' and that routing+approving together is forbidden.

drivers.where: Routing an in-policy invoice to finance-review is forbidden.
drivers.instance: Drives negative assertion mail_not_finance_review. Emailing finance-review@ means the model rejected an in-policy invoice; doing both branches zeroes strict.

drivers.where: update_invoice rejects a no-status call.
drivers.instance: An id-only update_invoice(id='INV-204') returns 'No fields to update', leaving inv_approved failed.

drivers.where: Three weighted assertions (0.34 / 0.33 / 0.33); all must pass.
drivers.instance: Partial/dense bands are reachable as 0.34 or 0.33 increments; mid-open lands ~0.34 (one step) while strict stays 0.0.

hard.ap_approval_threshold.gold_explanation: Latest AcmeRoast threshold = 5000 (2026-03-09) > 4200 -> Approve. Set INV-204 status Approved; log to ap-log@ with 'INV-204' and 'Approved'. Must NOT email finance-review@ (that would be the over-threshold branch, and doing both is forbidden).

hard.sla_route.title: SLA escalation routing
hard.sla_route.plain_summary: A support ticket has been open a while. Compute how long, compare it to the SLA limit for its priority, and if the SLA is breached, escalate it and page on-call -- without touching a deprecated mailbox. A second, non-breaching ticket is a decoy to leave alone.

inputs.label: The task prompt
inputs.detail: T-555 from NorthPeak opened 09:00, now 10:30; P1 tickets escalate within 1 hour; route by priority and elapsed time and log the escalation.

inputs.label: Tickets
inputs.detail: T-555 (P1, Open, opened_at 09:00, now 10:30) is the target. T-556 (P2, Open, same times) is a decoy that should be left alone (P2 SLA 240 min, 90 < 240, not breached).

inputs.label: The 'SLA escalation rules' email
inputs.detail: elapsed = now - opened_at; if elapsed exceeds the ticket's SLA the SLA is BREACHED -> set status Escalated and email oncall@ with the ticket id and 'SLA breach'; if not breached, leave it in backlog (do nothing); never email backlog@ (deprecated).

inputs.label: SLA table
inputs.detail: P1 = 60 minutes, P2 = 240 minutes (both as_of 2026-01-01).

tools.name: crm_list_tickets
tools.does: List the tickets for one account (surfaces T-555 and the T-556 decoy).

tools.name: crm_update_ticket
tools.does: Write a ticket's status; refuses an empty (no-status) update.

tools.name: tables_get_rows
tools.does: Read all rows of a named table plus a 'latest' pointer (the SLA table).

tools.name: mail_find
tools.does: Search the inbox by keyword.

tools.name: mail_get
tools.does: Read one inbox message's full body by id (the SLA rules email).

tools.name: mail_send
tools.does: Send an email; refuses a message with no subject and no body.

tools.name: finish
tools.does: Declare the task complete; changes nothing on its own.

hard.sla_route.success_criteria: Done right = T-555 status set to Escalated (elapsed 90 min > P1 SLA 60 min = breached); an email to oncall@ containing 'T-555' and 'SLA breach'; and NO email to backlog@. The P2 decoy T-556 is left untouched. All three assertions must hold for a strict pass.

drivers.where: The breach decision is duration math against a priority-specific limit.
drivers.instance: Drives ticket_escalated: elapsed = 10:30 - 09:00 = 90 min; P1 SLA = 60 min; 90 > 60 -> breached -> Escalated. Misreading the clock or using P2's 240-min limit takes the wrong branch.

drivers.where: Two open tickets on the same account; only the P1 is breached.
drivers.instance: T-556 (P2, 90 < 240 min) is a non-breach decoy. Escalating it, or emailing about it, is an extra write the task does not want.

drivers.where: The elapsed formula, the exact page text, and the backlog@ ban live in the inbox email.
drivers.instance: The model must read message m1 to learn to email oncall@ with 'T-555' and 'SLA breach' and to never touch backlog@.

drivers.where: Emailing the deprecated backlog@ mailbox is forbidden.
drivers.instance: Drives negative assertion mail_not_backlog. Routing a breached ticket to backlog@ zeroes strict on its own.

drivers.where: crm_update_ticket rejects a no-status call.
drivers.instance: An id-only crm_update_ticket(id='T-555') returns 'No fields to update', leaving ticket_escalated failed.

drivers.where: Three weighted assertions (0.34 / 0.33 / 0.33); all must pass.
drivers.instance: Same shape as ap_approval_threshold: partial bands of 0.33-0.34 are reachable while strict stays 0.0 until every check passes.

hard.sla_route.gold_explanation: T-555 is P1; elapsed 90 min (09:00 -> 10:30) > 60-min P1 SLA -> breached. Set T-555 Escalated; email oncall@ with 'T-555' and 'SLA breach'. Leave the P2 decoy T-556 alone. Must NOT email the deprecated backlog@.

easy.email_triage.title: Email triage
easy.email_triage.plain_summary: Read one support email and route it to exactly one of five mailboxes. One thing in, one label out -- the floor any model should clear.

inputs.label: The email
inputs.detail: A subject line and body -- e.g. 'URGENT: double charged on invoice 8841' / a complaint about being billed twice, blocking month-end close.

inputs.label: The label set (5 classes)
inputs.detail: billing_urgent, billing_normal, technical, sales_lead, spam -- pick exactly one.

classes.label: billing_urgent
classes.means: A billing fire with real impact/time pressure -- duplicate charge blocking payroll, account suspended before a demo, a 10x overcharge freezing the operating account. Action needed now.
classes.example_id: et-001 ('double charged on invoice 8841 ... blocking our month-end close')

classes.label: billing_normal
classes.means: A routine billing/admin request with no urgency -- confirm the next invoice date, send a receipt, update the card before next month, add a PO number. 'No rush' is the tell.
classes.example_id: et-002 ('confirm when my next invoice will be generated ... No rush.')

classes.label: technical
classes.means: A product not working -- crashes on CSV export, SSO login loop, charts not loading on Safari, webhooks stopped firing, API 500s. A bug or outage, not a money question.
classes.example_id: et-003 ('App crashes when I export to CSV')

classes.label: sales_lead
classes.means: A prospect or expansion with buying intent -- N seats, pricing, SSO/SOC 2, trial extension, nonprofit/partner pricing, API plan to unlock a purchase. Someone wants to buy or buy more.
classes.example_id: et-004 ('Interested in the Growth plan for 40 seats')

classes.label: spam
classes.means: Unsolicited junk or a phishing lure dressed up as business -- 'you won a gift card', 'domain expiring, pay now', 'invoice.zip, enable macros', 'crypto doubling event'. Catch the lure, don't treat it as real.
classes.example_id: et-005 ('You won a $1000 gift card!!! click here')

easy.email_triage.success_criteria: Done right = the predicted label exactly matches the gold mailbox for that email. Scored as exact-match; strict and dense are the same here (one label, nothing partial).

drivers.where: billing_urgent vs billing_normal share the same topic.
drivers.instance: et-001 (duplicate charge blocking close) vs et-002 (confirm invoice date, 'no rush') -- both billing; only urgency/impact splits them. Boundary rows like et-010 even cross topic into sales_lead.

drivers.where: Spam that imitates a real business email.
drivers.instance: Boundary spam et-012 ('newsletter: AcmeRoast spring blends'), et-015 ('domain expiring, pay $14.99'), and et-057 ('invoice.zip, enable macros') must land as spam, not billing/technical.

drivers.where: A handful of rows are flagged boundary:true in the fixture.
drivers.instance: et-009, et-010, et-011, et-012, et-015, et-025, et-030 and a few more are the near-edge cases; the small model may slip one (the roster shows reward 0.95 as honest texture).

easy.email_triage.gold_explanation: Exact-match routing. The representative row et-001 is a duplicate charge blocking month-end close -> billing_urgent. A human reads the subject and knows in two seconds; so should any model. Reported qualitatively as 'all models pass' (the holdout is too thin for a stable >=0.95 figure).

medium.relevance_grade.title: Search relevance grading
medium.relevance_grade.plain_summary: Given a shopper's search and one product, label how the product relates to the search: Exact, Substitute, Complement, or Irrelevant. One turn, but it needs judgment a 2B model doesn't reliably have.

inputs.label: The search query
inputs.detail: What the shopper typed -- e.g. 'running shoes'.

inputs.label: The product
inputs.detail: One catalog item to grade against that query -- e.g. 'TravelPro ankle socks, 3-pack'.

inputs.label: The label set (4 classes)
inputs.detail: Exact, Substitute, Complement, Irrelevant -- pick exactly one.

classes.label: Exact
classes.means: The product IS what the shopper searched for -- a running shoe for 'running shoes'.

classes.label: Substitute
classes.means: A different item that could REPLACE the searched one -- trail shoes for 'running shoes'.

classes.label: Complement
classes.means: Goes WITH the search but isn't the same item -- ankle socks for 'running shoes'. You buy them together; you don't swap one for the other.

classes.label: Irrelevant
classes.means: Unrelated to the search -- a coffee mug for 'running shoes'.

medium.relevance_grade.success_criteria: Done right = the predicted relevance label matches gold for that query/product pair. Scored as a rate across many items (macro-F1), not a single row; the headline metric is Complement recall.

worked_example.why: You wear socks WITH running shoes, not instead of them, so the right tag is Complement. The small model reasons 'both go on feet -> substitute' and treats them as interchangeable.

drivers.where: Complement vs Substitute is a conceptual, not surface, distinction.
drivers.instance: The running-shoes/ankle-socks pair: both relate to feet, but one is bought-with (Complement) and one is swapped-for (Substitute). This single boundary is where the small model collapses -- Complement recall ~6% vs ~62% for the capable band.

drivers.where: MEDIUM is the one rung scored and reported as a rate, with a cheap-recovery story.
drivers.instance: Untuned 2B macro-F1 ~0.29; capable band ~0.65. One short RL pass lifts the 2B to ~0.55 macro-F1 and Complement recall 6% -> ~62% for about $1.17 (illustrative). The shown row is one representative mislabel for texture, not the claim.

medium.relevance_grade.gold_explanation: The relationship is graded by concept, not keyword overlap. 'Running shoes' + 'ankle socks' = Complement (bought together, not interchangeable). The claim is the Complement-recall rate across many items -- small-local ~6% vs capable ~62% -- not this one row. P0 note: MEDIUM is a pre-baked beat; its live environment is deferred to P1.

GENERALIZATION_NOTE: This same five-part anatomy (plain_summary, inputs, tools, success_criteria, drivers) is the model the dissector hands to Door A (understand-workload). For a USER's own task: plain_summary = the one-line purpose; inputs = what the model actually sees; tools = the actions it can take (empty for a single-turn classifier); success_criteria = how 'done right' is checked; drivers = the specific things that make it hard, each glossed from the shared GLOSSARY and tagged to a concrete instance in their data (a recency-trapped table, a forbidden recipient, a multi-hop lookup, a subtle class boundary). The glossary terms are workload-agnostic; only the where/instance fields are fixture-specific, so the structure carries over unchanged when pointed at real traces.
